title: Homogeneous coordinates for continuous cochains with topological coefficients
statement:
Let $E$ be a topological field [def-weil-field], $J$ a topological group, and $V$ a topological $E$-vector space with a jointly continuous $E$-linear $J$-action. Let $B^n(J,V)$ consist of the jointly continuous functions $F:J^{n+1}\to V$ satisfying $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ for every $a\in J$, with pointwise $E$-vector space structure and differential
$$(\delta F)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{n+1}).$$
Let $C^n(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$, $C^0(J,V)=V$, with differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n),$$
including $(dv)(g)=gv-v$. These are ordinary complexes of abstract $E$-vector spaces, extended by zero in negative degrees. In the derived category $D(E\text{-Vect})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there is a natural isomorphism $Q(B^\bullet(J,V))\simeq Q(C^\bullet(J,V))$, represented by an actual $E$-linear cochain isomorphism $\Phi:B^\bullet(J,V)\to C^\bullet(J,V)$ with inverse $\Psi$, given by
$$(\Phi_nF)(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=F(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n),$$
$$(\Psi_nf)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=x_0 f(x_0^{-1}x_1,x_1^{-1}x_2,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n).$$
Thus $\Phi_{n+1}\delta=d\Phi_n$ and $\Psi_{n+1}d=\delta\Psi_n$; in degree zero $\Phi_0F=F(1)$ and $\Psi_0v(x)=xv$. Both cochain isomorphisms commute with continuous equivariant $E$-linear coefficient maps and with restriction along continuous homomorphisms of topological groups (using the restricted action on $V$). No compactness, discreteness, completeness, or local compactness hypothesis is imposed.

Its pointwise vector spaces and inverse linear maps are precisely B^n, C^n, Φ_n and Ψ_n in the item, including evaluation at 1 and x↦xv in degree zero. This constructs the actual maps on jointly continuous functions without a compact-open exponential law.

proof.text: The differential lemma makes δ and d well-defined linear maps, proves δ²=0 and gives Φ_{n+1}δ=dΦ_n with the displayed signs, including dv(g)=gv−v. Using the inverse identities of the coordinate equivalence gives d=Φ_{n+1}δΨ_n. Therefore d²=Φ_{n+2}δ(Ψ_{n+1}Φ_{n+1})δΨ_n=0, and Ψ_{n+1}d=δΨ_n. Extend B,C and both arrows by zero in negative degrees. The differential from degree −1 is zero, so the resulting arrows are mutually inverse cochain maps in every integer degree.

proof.text: For restriction along a continuous h:H→J, the action on V is jointly continuous: compose (a,v)↦(h(a),v) with the given J-action. Apply the simultaneous naturality lemma with u=id_V and this restricted action; its intertwining hypothesis is the identity h(a)v=h(a)v. For a continuous equivariant coefficient map u, apply it with h=id_J. In both cases it supplies the two differential identities and both coordinate squares. Extend b,c by zero in negative degrees; these equalities still hold, giving naturality of both inverse cochain maps.

proof.text: Apply the localization functor Q of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to these abstract E-vector-space complexes and arrows. Functoriality gives Q(Ψ)Q(Φ)=Q(ΨΦ)=id_{Q(B)} and Q(Φ)Q(Ψ)=id_{Q(C)}. Hence Q(Φ) with inverse Q(Ψ) is the asserted isomorphism in D(E-Vect), represented by the actual cochain isomorphism. Applying Q to the cochain naturality equalities proves derived naturality as well. This is a derived-category isomorphism, not merely an assertion about cohomology groups.
